every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not

claims.claim: The query SMILES corresponds to flumazenil; no direct flumazenil-specific oral bioavailability record is supplied in the visible cards.

The only cirrhosis-matched record is pentoxifylline, with absolute oral bioavailability 0.71 ± 0.24 in cirrhotic patients after a 400 mg sustained-release tablet, well above the 20% threshold; L2 records repeat this value.
Structurally related ondansetron has absolute oral bioavailability of approximately 50–70% in humans across multiple records, supporting F ≥ 20% for the query.

L6 records show that the closely related imidazobenzodiazepine ethyl ester XHE-III-74EE (M01) is stable in human and mouse liver microsomes and S9 fractions for 1 hour with a predicted half-life of several hours, supporting low hepatic first-pass for this chemotype.

C68 shows ondansetron, alosetron and GR87442 have comparable hepatic clearances in human hepatocytes, consistent with ondansetron's high oral bioavailability; it does not provide a numeric clearance for the query.
The physicochemical prior is favorable for oral absorption (MW 303 Da, logD 1.77, no HBD, neutral at physiological pH, moderate TPSA), supporting but not proving F ≥ 20%.
No affirmative threshold-relevant evidence for F < 20% is present.
